name: ExpandingPanels
whenToUse: A landing section that shows three to five things side by side: collections, use cases, plans. Prefer tones over photos: pictures make the row heavy and noisy.

whenNotToUse.text: Text people need to read side by side or compare
Questions and answers, settings, long content
More than about five panels — the strips get too narrow to read

anatomy.description: a bright system fill (`tone`: primary, success, info, danger) with its own text color — no gradient, no darkening; or, sparingly, a picture under a dark gradient. Open, it takes about five times a strip’s width.
a button in a heading (`titleAs`); runs up the strip when closed, sits above the text when open.
a line or two and at most one link, shown only in the open panel.

do.caption: Titles fit the strip; the open text reads at a glance.
do.example: <Tile>4 panels, short titles, one line each</Tile>

dont.caption: Strips too thin to read and text cut off — use a grid.

a11y: An accordion: each title is a button with aria-expanded in a heading; the open text is a region named by it. One open at a time.
Hover (mouse) and keyboard focus open a panel; leaving does not close it, so nothing flickers. Closed text is inert.
The row keeps its height — only widths change, nothing below the row moves.
Below 768px the panels stack and open downwards, titles horizontal.
prefers-reduced-motion: the panels switch without sliding.

props.name: height
props.description: Row height on wide screens (CSS length, default 28rem).

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the index of the panel that opens.

props.name: titleAs
props.description: Heading level of the titles (default h3).
